subject.title: Dublin Unified School District — Measure I (Parcel Tax Measure)

text: “Shall the measure to support quality education, provide local funding that cannot be taken by the State, maintain small class sizes, attract/retain quality teachers, and provide enhanced science, technology, engineering, visual and performing arts, reading, writing, and math programs, by renewing the expiring $96 school parcel tax, adding $48 per parcel, providing approximately $2,900,000 annually for nine years, with senior exemptions, annual inflation adjustments, independent oversight, and all funds locally controlled, be adopted?”

analysis.title: Impartial Analysis
analysis.by: Andrea L. Weddle, Interim County Counsel The above statement is an impartial analysis of Measure I, which is printed in full in this sample ballot pamphlet. If you desire an additional copy of the measure, please call the Elections Official’s office at (510) 272-6933 and a copy will be mailed at no cost to you. You may also access the full text of the measure on the Alameda County website at the following address: www.acvote.org.

text:
ANALYSIS BY THE COUNTY COUNSEL FOR THE COUNTY OF ALAMEDA OF A DUBLIN UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT SPECIAL PARCEL TAX MEASURE
Measure I (“Measure”), a Dublin Unified School District (“District”) special parcel tax measure, seeks voter approval to authorize the District to levy a nine-year special parcel tax, beginning on July 1, 2027, at the initial uniform rate of $144 per parcel per year in the first applicable tax year, then adjusted each tax year thereafter by the percentage change in the consumer price index to account for inflation on the cost of delivering programs and services supported by the parcel tax. 
The District estimates the parcel tax, if passed, will provide approximately $2,900,000 annually. The District will use the revenue only for the purposes listed in the Measure, which include, but are not limited to: attracting and retaining qualified teachers and staff; maintaining small class sizes; providing enhanced science, technology, visual and performing arts, reading, writing, and math programs; supporting student wellness and academic intervention; and maintaining instructional materials, classroom technology, and school library collections. 
If passed, as of July 1, 2027, the parcel tax will supersede and replace the District’s Measure E, an existing parcel tax passed in 2019. If the measure fails, Measure E would continue until June 30, 2028, when it will cease to be in effect. 
In addition to properties otherwise exempt from property taxes, the following people may apply to the District for exemptions on residential parcels owned and occupied as a principal residence: persons 65 years or older; persons receiving Supplemental Security Income for a disability; and persons receiving Social Security Disability Insurance Benefits who meet specified income requirements.
The Measure contains certain accountability provisions, including requiring the District to deposit parcel tax proceeds in a separate account, produce an annual report to the District’s governing board from the District’s chief fiscal officer detailing the amount of funds collected and expended and the status of any projects funded by the proceeds, and conduct an annual financial audit by the District’s governing board to ensure parcel tax proceeds are spent for educational purposes. The District’s governing board will also appoint a citizen oversight committee to review the District’s use of parcel tax proceeds to ensure that they are expended for the purposes listed in the Measure. 
A school district has the authority to levy special taxes upon approval by two-thirds of the votes cast on the special tax proposal. (Cal. Const. art. XIII A, § 4; art. XIII C, § 2; Cal. Gov’t Code §§ 50075-50077, 50079, 53722.) If two-thirds of the qualified electors voting on this Measure do not vote for approval, it will fail, and the District will not be authorized to levy the special parcel tax.
This Measure is placed on the ballot by the governing board of the District.
